content:
Tiredness is common with arthritis and frailty. The challenge is resting without losing strength.

This guide covers balancing rest and activity. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Rest vs inactivity

Planned rest helps you pace. Long periods of not moving can weaken muscles and stiffen joints.

Naps

  • Keep naps short.
  • Avoid late-afternoon naps if they disturb night sleep.

Breaking up sitting

  • Stand or move every hour or so if you can.
  • Seated exercises during TV adverts.
  • Make a drink or walk to the window.

Making a home work harder for you

  • Place things so you get up for them.
  • Use a chair you can rise from easily.
  • Keep a walking aid within reach.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is it bad to nap?

Short naps are fine for many people.

How much should I move?

Little and often; ask a physiotherapist.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Insomnia
  • NHS: Tiredness and fatigue
